narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`task reconcile:issues -- --apply-lifecycle-fixes` git-moves closed-issue xBRIEFs `active/` -> `completed/` without a `scope:complete` runTransition stamp. `verify:completed-write-guard` then fails `task check` / release Step 5: "added under completed/ without a runTransition write" and "renamed away from active/ with no paired stamped destination."

Observed on the v0.118.1 cut. Five UAT residual briefs from PR 4492 squash (`#3849` `#3918` `#4161` `#4204` `#4218`) landed in `active/` on origin/master after merge. Reconcile moved them. Step 5 failed. Recovery was `task scope:complete -- <completed-path> --merge-commit 46df9e495 --pr 4492` (restamp `deliveryDisposition=delivered`), then a third commit, then Step 5 passed.

Release Phase 1 tells the operator to run apply-lifecycle-fixes as the canonical clean path before `task release`. That path currently authors the exact tree the write-guard refuses.

## Expected

Apply-lifecycle-fixes either:

- writes the same runTransition stamp `scope:complete` writes, so the write-guard accepts `R active->completed`, or
- refuses to move and prints the leftover-complete command (`scope:complete --merge-commit <sha> --pr <n>`).

## Actual

Reconcile moves. Guard fails. Operator must restamp by hand before the cut can proceed.

## Acceptance

- After apply-lifecycle-fixes, `task verify:completed-write-guard` is green on that change set (stamp present), or the move is not performed and the printed recovery can succeed.
- A test pins the stamp (or the refuse + printed command) for a closed-issue active/ brief.
- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`.
- Does not weaken the write-guard to accept unstamped husks.

## Out of scope

- `#3819` stamp-exists-but-disposition-invalid.
- `#4001` superseded proposal routed to completed/ instead of cancelled/.
- Recutting the five v0.118.1 leftover completes.

## Origin

v0.118.1 Phase 1 reconcile then Step 5. Refs #3819, #4001, #3476, #4265.

## Verdict

The named refutation-target survives. I could not break the causal chain.

`applyLifecycleFixes` (`packages/core/src/intake/reconcile-issues.ts`) git-moves a closed-issue brief into `completed/` after writing `plan.status`, envelope `updated`, and item statuses. It never calls `stampLifecycleWrite` / `runTransition`. `stampLifecycleWrite` is only invoked from `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts`. `hasTransitionWrite` then stays false (no `lifecycleWrite`, no `metadata.completedAt`, status is `completed` not `failed`). `evaluateCompletedWriteGuard` therefore emits both observed strings: "added under completed/ without a runTransition write" and "renamed away from active/ with no paired stamped destination". Reproduced against the dispatch-SHA predicates: `fitsCompleted=false`. Release Phase 1 item 5 and pipeline Step 3 still name `--apply-lifecycle-fixes` as the clean path; Step 5 `task check` includes `verify:completed-write-guard` on both framework and consumer gate lists.

The defect is real. The two-option Expected set is not yet bindable as written.

## 1. Either-or currently permits forging the #3679 fingerprint

class: blocks-the-design

evidence: `packages/core/src/scope/lifecycle-write.ts` states the stamp "only records that runTransition wrote the blob." Callers at this SHA: `transition.ts` complete / fail / cancel / restamp. `applyLifecycleFixes` is not a caller. Out-of-scope #3819 is still open: "the completed-artifact guard checks that a transition stamp exists, not that its disposition is valid." `verify:completed-tracked` is not on the check graph, so a minted fingerprint would make Step 5 green while leaving disposition unchecked. Expected option 1 ("writes the same runTransition stamp") can be read as `stampLifecycleWrite` inside apply.

failure mode: An implementer mints `plan.metadata.lifecycleWrite` in the reconcile sweep. The write-guard accepts `R active->completed`. The blob is still not a `runTransition` write. That is the husk #3679 forbids, with the token the guard trusts. It is also the #3819 shape this issue parked. GitHub `state_reason` becomes authority to mint a trusted fingerprint (untrusted issue state to shared xbrief tree).

disposition: The either-or cannot bind. Drop fingerprint-only mint from the allowed set. Bind leftover-complete (option 2, corrected below) or recut the stamp's writer set as a deliberate #3679 amendment, which pulls #3819 into this issue. Calling `runTransition("complete")` from apply is not a third silent member: it needs #3041 delivery evidence apply does not have, and GitHub-closed is not that evidence.

## 2. Option 2 printed command is the post-move restamp

class: sharpens-framing

evidence: Observed recovery was `task scope:complete -- <completed-path> --merge-commit 46df9e495 --pr 4492` after apply had already moved the files. `runTransition` restamp is only legal when `currentFolder === "completed"` (`transition.ts`). `complete` from a non-completed folder requires `active/`. `verify:orphan-active` already prints `task scope:complete -- ${orphan.path}` for this class (`packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts`). Delivery-gate remediation already names `--merge-commit` / `--pr` when the complete is code-bearing (`delivery-evidence.ts`). Phase 1 item 5 and Step 3 still say the recovery is re-running apply.

failure mode: Refuse-and-print the Expected command against a completed-path: the file is still in `active/`, restamp refuses, leftover-complete does not succeed. Re-run apply as Phase 1/Step 3 still instruct: apply refuses again, Section (c) mismatch remains, cut stalls unless `--allow-vbrief-drift`. Resolving SHA/PR from GitHub inside apply reopens the #4269 per-issue fetch blast.

disposition: Under refuse, print the existing active-path leftover-complete line (orphan-active), not a restamp of a file that was never moved. Let the delivery gate ask for `--merge-commit` / `--pr`. Retarget Phase 1 / Step 3 recovery copy for this class to that verb. Apply becomes a detector/printer here, not the mover.

## 3. Stop 1 write-back has no pain list

class: sharpens-framing

evidence: Ceiling comment 5664447431 has `design-critique: warranted, because ...` and `refutation-target:` and no operative `pain:` list. Bind evaluator fails closed as `missing-pain` when the Stop 1 list is missing or vacuous.

failure mode: An all-accept map still cannot complete the arc. The product finding is not the blocker; the warrant record is.

disposition: Parent posts a superseding Stop 1 warrant with a closed `pain:` list (at least P1 = write-guard refuses the tree Phase 1 just authored). Do not edit 5664447431 in place.

## 4. Cancelled dest from active/ is the same unstamped move

class: footnote

`destinationFolder` routes `NOT_PLANNED` / `DUPLICATE` to `cancelled/`. Write-guard pairing for `active/` to `cancelled/` requires `lifecycleWrite.action=cancel`; status-only cancelled dests do not pair (tests in `completed-write-guard.test.ts`). Same Step 5 failure, different folder. Observed v0.118.1 residuals were `COMPLETED` to `completed/`. Do not expand into #4001 (proposed/pending leftover recovery). If bind is refuse-for-unstamped-terminal-moves, say whether cancelled is in or out.

## Injection / swarm lens

This target changes authority (who may mint `lifecycleWrite`), untrusted input (GitHub closed / `state_reason`), and shared state (xbrief lifecycle tree). GitHub-closed must not write the fingerprint `runTransition` owns. Option 2-as-detector keeps GitHub as a report trigger. Fingerprint mint does not.

## Road not taken

Rejected: mint `stampLifecycleWrite` inside apply so Step 5 goes green.

Steelman: #3679 already split fingerprint from delivery (does not change `verify:completed-tracked`). #3819 exists because that split was deliberate. Reconcile already writes complete-shaped `plan.status` / items without `runTransition`. One more field is the cheapest cut-unblock, and parking #3819 is honest.

What would flip: a recorded recut that apply is a second authorized writer of `lifecycleWrite`, with #3819 in scope. Absent that recut, mint is a backdoor.

Existing mechanisms to reuse, not replace: `scope:complete` / restamp, `verify:orphan-active` printer, leftover-land PR (#3476), swarm Phase 6 complete/finalize. Do not add a SHA resolver to apply.
